explanation.en: Gershon was Levi's eldest son and ancestor of a major Levitical clan. Numbers 3:25 assigns the Gershonites care of the tabernacle coverings, curtains, and hangings during Israel's journeys.
explanation.zh: 革顺是利未的长子，也是利未一个主要宗族的先祖。民数记3:25把会幕的罩棚、幔子和帷子交给革顺族在旅途中照管。

sampleVerse.text: And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the tabernacle of the congregation shall be the tabernacle, and the tent, the covering thereof, and the hanging for the door of the tabernacle of the congregation,

explanation.en: Jezebel was the Sidonian princess who married Ahab and used royal power to promote Baal worship and persecute the LORD's prophets. First Kings 16:31 links Ahab's marriage to her with his deliberate service of Baal.
explanation.zh: 耶洗别是嫁给亚哈的西顿公主，她利用王权推动巴力崇拜并迫害耶和华的先知。列王纪上16:31把亚哈娶她与他主动事奉巴力直接相连。

sampleVerse.text: And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.

explanation.en: Ekron was the northernmost of the five principal Philistine cities. First Samuel 5:10 records the captured ark being sent there, where the terrified inhabitants protested after judgment had already struck Ashdod and Gath.
explanation.zh: 以革伦是非利士五座主要城市中最北的一座。撒母耳记上5:10记载被掳的约柜送到那里；在亚实突和迦特已遭灾后，居民因恐惧而抗议。

sampleVerse.text: Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.

explanation.en: Achish was the Philistine king of Gath who twice received David while he fled from Saul. First Samuel 27:2 records David and six hundred men seeking refuge with him, beginning a morally complex period in Philistine territory.
explanation.zh: 亚吉是非利士迦特王，大卫逃避扫罗时两次投奔他。撒母耳记上27:2记载大卫带六百人寻求他的庇护，由此开始一段在非利士地处境复杂的时期。

sampleVerse.text: And David arose, and he passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.

explanation.en: Ithamar was Aaron's youngest son and one of the surviving priests after Nadab and Abihu died. Exodus 28:1 names him among Aaron's sons set apart for priestly service, from whose line later priests also descended.
explanation.zh: 以他玛是亚伦最小的儿子，也是拿答、亚比户死后仍存的祭司之一。出埃及记28:1把他列在分别出来担任祭司的亚伦众子中，后来也有祭司出自他的谱系。

sampleVerse.text: And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.

explanation.en: Naomi was Ruth's Israelite mother-in-law, who returned to Bethlehem after losing her husband and two sons in Moab. Ruth 1:20 records her asking to be called Mara, meaning bitter, honestly voicing grief that the rest of the book gradually answers with restoration.
explanation.zh: 拿俄米是路得的以色列婆婆，在摩押失去丈夫和两个儿子后回到伯利恒。路得记1:20记载她要求别人称她“玛拉”，意为苦；她诚实表达的悲痛，在后文逐渐得到恢复的回应。

sampleVerse.text: And she said unto them, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.

explanation.en: Abijah son of Rehoboam was the second king of Judah after the kingdom divided and is also called Abijam. Second Chronicles 13:1 dates his accession during Jeroboam's reign, placing his short rule within the continuing conflict between north and south.
explanation.zh: 罗波安的儿子亚比雅是王国分裂后的第二位犹大王，也称亚比央。历代志下13:1把他的登基定在耶罗波安年间，使其短暂统治处于南北两国持续冲突之中。

sampleVerse.text: Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam began Abijah to reign over Judah.

explanation.en: Ahikam son of Shaphan was a royal official and father of the later governor Gedaliah. Jeremiah 26:24 credits his protection with keeping Jeremiah from execution by a hostile crowd.
explanation.zh: 沙番的儿子亚希甘是王室官员，也是后来省长基大利的父亲。耶利米书26:24指出，是他的保护使耶利米没有被敌对群众处死。

sampleVerse.text: Nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.

explanation.en: The Negeb is the dry southern region of Canaan crossed by routes between Palestine and Egypt; the KJV commonly calls it 'the south.' Genesis 13:1 records Abram returning from Egypt into this region with his household and possessions.
explanation.zh: 尼革夫是迦南南部干旱地区，巴勒斯坦与埃及之间的道路经过这里；KJV 通常把它译作“南地”。创世记13:1记载亚伯兰带着家人和财物从埃及回到这片地区。

sampleVerse.text: And Abram went up out of Egypt, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the south.

explanation.en: The Nile is Egypt's life-giving river, usually called simply 'the river' in the KJV. Exodus 7:20 records its water turning to blood before Pharaoh, striking at the resource on which Egypt's life and power depended.
explanation.zh: 尼罗河是维系埃及生命的大河，在 KJV 中通常只称“河”。出埃及记7:20记载河水在法老面前变成血，击中了埃及生存与权势所倚赖的资源。

sampleVerse.text: And Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.

explanation.en: Susa was a Persian royal capital called Shushan in the KJV and the main setting of Esther's story. Esther 1:2 places Ahasuerus on his throne in the palace there, establishing the imperial court in which Esther would intervene.
explanation.zh: 苏萨是波斯王都，KJV 称为书珊，也是以斯帖故事的主要背景。以斯帖记1:2记载亚哈随鲁王在当地宫中坐王位，确立了以斯帖后来出面干预的帝国宫廷环境。

sampleVerse.text: That in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which was in Shushan the palace,

explanation.en: To call may mean naming, summoning, appointing, or crying out to God in prayer and trust. Romans 10:13 promises salvation to everyone who calls upon the Lord's name, expressing dependence rather than self-rescue.
explanation.zh: 呼叫可以指命名、召集、委任，也可指人在祷告和信靠中向上帝呼求。罗马书10:13应许凡求告主名的都必得救，表达的是倚靠上帝，而非自我拯救。

sampleVerse.text: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

explanation.en: A river is a flowing watercourse that sustains life, marks boundaries, and shapes many biblical journeys. Genesis 2:10 describes a river watering Eden before dividing into four heads, presenting abundant water as part of the created garden.
explanation.zh: 河流是不断流动的水道，维持生命、划定边界，也塑造许多圣经旅程。创世记2:10描述一条河从伊甸流出滋润园子，随后分为四道，显出受造园地中丰盛的水源。

sampleVerse.text: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.

explanation.en: Host can mean a vast organized multitude, especially an army or the ordered array of heaven and earth. Genesis 2:1 says the heavens, earth, and all their host were finished, gathering the fullness of creation under one term.
explanation.zh: Host 可指庞大而有秩序的群体，尤其是军队，或天地间排列整齐的万有。创世记2:1说天地和其中的万象都造齐了，用一个词概括创造的完整。

sampleVerse.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.

explanation.en: Stone was a common building material, boundary marker, memorial, weapon, and rich biblical symbol. First Peter 2:5 calls believers living stones being built into a spiritual house around Christ, the chosen cornerstone.
explanation.zh: 石头在圣经时代是常见的建筑材料、界标、纪念物和武器，也具有丰富象征意义。彼得前书2:5称信徒为活石，围绕蒙拣选的房角石基督，被建造成属灵的殿。

sampleVerse.text: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

explanation.en: A judge decides disputes, while Israel's judges were also leaders raised up to deliver the people before the monarchy. Judges 2:16 says the LORD raised such judges to rescue Israel from those who plundered them.
explanation.zh: 审判官裁断争议；在君王制度以前，以色列的士师也兼任蒙召拯救百姓的领袖。士师记2:16说耶和华兴起士师，救百姓脱离抢夺他们的人。

sampleVerse.text: Nevertheless the LORD raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.

explanation.en: Sheep were central to biblical pastoral life and depend heavily on a shepherd for food, guidance, and protection. Psalm 23:1 calls the LORD the psalmist's shepherd, using that dependence to express confident trust in God's care.
explanation.zh: 羊是圣经牧养生活的重要牲畜，高度倚赖牧人供应、引导和保护。诗篇23:1称耶和华为诗人的牧者，以羊的倚赖表达对上帝照顾的坚定信靠。

sampleVerse.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

explanation.en: Beast is an older broad term for land animals and can also become a prophetic symbol of brutal political power. Genesis 1:24 places the beasts of the earth among the living creatures God commands the earth to bring forth.
explanation.zh: Beast 是泛指陆地动物的古典用语，在预言中也可象征残暴的政治权势。创世记1:24把地上的走兽列在上帝命令大地产生的活物之中。

sampleVerse.text: And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.

explanation.en: A city wall provided defense, controlled access, and visibly marked a community's security. Nehemiah 2:17 calls Jerusalem's survivors to rebuild their broken wall so the city would no longer remain a reproach.
explanation.zh: 城墙用于防御、控制出入，也明显标示群体的安全状态。尼希米记2:17呼召耶路撒冷余民重建破毁的城墙，使城不再受羞辱。

sampleVerse.text: Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.

explanation.en: A throne is the seat and symbol of royal authority; God's throne represents his sovereign rule and judgment. Revelation 4:2 centers John's heavenly vision on a throne and the One seated upon it, placing divine kingship above every earthly power.
explanation.zh: 宝座是君王权柄的座位和象征；上帝的宝座代表祂至高的统治与审判。启示录4:2把约翰的天上异象集中在宝座和坐在其上的主，使神圣王权高过一切地上势力。

sampleVerse.text: And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne.

explanation.en: Grace is God's undeserved favor that forgives, restores, and empowers rather than a reward earned by human merit. Ephesians 2:8 says salvation comes by grace through faith as God's gift, excluding works as its cause.
explanation.zh: 恩典是上帝并非按人功劳赐下的恩惠，带来赦免、恢复和能力，而不是人赚得的报酬。以弗所书2:8说救恩本乎恩、因着信，是上帝的礼物，不以人的行为为成因。

sampleVerse.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:

explanation.en: Peter was a fisherman called by Jesus and a leading apostle whose denial was followed by restoration and bold witness. Acts 2:14 records him standing with the Twelve to preach at Pentecost, marking his public role in the early church.
explanation.zh: 彼得原是蒙耶稣呼召的渔夫，后来成为重要使徒；他虽曾否认主，却得恢复并勇敢见证。使徒行传2:14记载他在五旬节与十一使徒一同站起讲道，显出他在初代教会中的公开角色。

sampleVerse.text: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judaea, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:

explanation.en: East is the direction of sunrise and often locates lands such as Arabia, Mesopotamia, or Persia from Israel's viewpoint. Matthew 2:2 records wise men from the east seeking the newborn King after seeing his star.
explanation.zh: 东是日出的方向；从以色列视角看，也常用来定位阿拉伯、美索不达米亚或波斯等地。马太福音2:2记载来自东方的博士看见新王之星，前来寻找祂。

sampleVerse.text: Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.

explanation.en: Cattle broadly refers to domesticated livestock and was a major measure of agricultural wealth in biblical society. Genesis 13:2 notes Abraham's abundance of cattle alongside silver and gold, showing the material scale of his household.
explanation.zh: Cattle 泛指家养牲畜，在圣经社会中是衡量农牧财富的重要标准。创世记13:2把亚伯拉罕众多牲畜与金银并列，显出他家业的规模。

sampleVerse.text: And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.

explanation.en: Heathen is an older KJV term for the nations or peoples outside Israel, not a statement that any ethnicity has less human worth. Psalm 115:2 voices those nations asking where Israel's God is, before contrasting their idols with the sovereign God in heaven.
explanation.zh: Heathen 是 KJV 中指以色列以外“列国”或“外邦人”的旧词，并非宣称某个族群的人性价值较低。诗篇115:2写列国追问以色列的上帝在哪里，随后把他们的偶像与在天掌权的上帝对比。

sampleVerse.text: Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is now their God?

explanation.en: South can indicate direction, but in many Old Testament passages it translates Negeb, the dry region below Judah. Genesis 12:9 records Abram journeying toward that southern country as he moved through Canaan.
explanation.zh: 南可以表示方向；旧约许多经文中，它也翻译 Negeb，即犹大以南的干旱地区。创世记12:9记载亚伯兰在迦南迁行，渐渐往南地去。

sampleVerse.text: And Abram journeyed, going on still toward the south.

explanation.en: John most prominently names John the Baptist, who prepared for Jesus, and the apostle John, one of the Twelve. Matthew 3:1 introduces the Baptist preaching repentance in Judea's wilderness before Christ's public ministry.
explanation.zh: 约翰主要指为耶稣预备道路的施洗约翰，也指十二使徒之一的使徒约翰。马太福音3:1介绍施洗约翰在犹太旷野传讲悔改，时间在基督公开传道之前。

sampleVerse.text: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea,

explanation.en: Money is a medium of exchange and a practical tool, but Scripture repeatedly warns against making wealth one's master. First Timothy 6:10 identifies love of money—not money itself—as a root that draws people into many evils and sorrows.
explanation.zh: 金钱是交换媒介和实用工具，但圣经屡次警告人不可让财富成为主人。提摩太前书6:10指出，万恶之根是贪爱钱财，而不是钱本身；这种贪爱使人陷入许多罪恶和愁苦。

sampleVerse.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

explanation.en: Captain is a leader placed over soldiers or guards and may denote ranks from unit commander to army chief. Joshua 5:14 presents the captain of the LORD's host before Joshua, shifting attention from human command to God's authority over Israel's battle.
explanation.zh: Captain 指统领士兵或护卫的长官，职位可从小队领袖到全军统帅。约书亚记5:14描写耶和华军队的元帅向约书亚显现，使焦点从人的指挥转向上帝对以色列争战的权柄。

sampleVerse.text: And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my lord unto his servant?

explanation.en: A valley is low ground between hills or mountains and may suggest fertility, travel, danger, or battle. Psalm 23:4 uses the darkest valley as a picture of mortal danger where the shepherd's presence removes fear.
explanation.zh: 山谷是丘陵或山脉之间的低地，可让人想到肥沃、旅途、危险或争战。诗篇23:4用幽暗山谷描绘致命险境，而牧者的同在使人不再惧怕。

sampleVerse.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

explanation.en: A camp is a temporary organized settlement, especially the tribal encampment used during Israel's wilderness journey. Numbers 2:2 orders every tribe around the tabernacle under its own standard, placing worship at the community's center.
explanation.zh: 营是有组织的临时住处，尤其指以色列在旷野旅程中的支派营地。民数记2:2安排各支派按旗号围绕会幕扎营，把敬拜置于群体生活的中心。

sampleVerse.text: Every man of the children of Israel shall pitch by his own standard, with the ensign of their father's house: far off about the tabernacle of the congregation shall they pitch.

explanation.en: The Sabbath is the seventh day set apart by God at creation for rest, worship, mercy, and remembrance. Exodus 20:10 identifies that day as the Sabbath of the LORD and extends its rest to children, servants, visitors, and animals.
explanation.zh: 安息日是上帝在创造时分别出来的第七日，用于安息、敬拜、怜悯和记念。出埃及记20:10明确称第七日为归耶和华的安息日，并把安息延伸到儿女、仆婢、寄居者和牲畜。

sampleVerse.text: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

explanation.en: A witness gives testimony about what has been seen or known and bears serious responsibility for truth. Deuteronomy 19:15 requires two or three witnesses to establish a charge, guarding judgment against one unsupported accusation.
explanation.zh: 见证人就自己所见所知作证，因此承担严肃的诚实责任。申命记19:15要求凭两三个人的口才可定案，防止审判只建立在一项未经支持的指控上。

sampleVerse.text: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.

explanation.en: Clean can describe physical purity, moral innocence, or the ceremonial and dietary distinctions God gave Israel. Leviticus 11:47 concludes the food laws by requiring discernment between clean and unclean animals, connecting holiness with choices in everyday life.
explanation.zh: 洁净可以指身体清洁、道德无罪，也指上帝赐给以色列的礼仪和饮食区分。利未记11:47以分辨洁净与不洁净的动物总结食物条例，把圣洁与日常生活中的选择联系起来。

sampleVerse.text: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.

explanation.en: Biblical hope is confident expectation grounded in God's character and promise rather than uncertain wishing. Titus 2:13 directs that hope toward the glorious appearing of Jesus Christ, making the Second Coming its personal focus.
explanation.zh: 圣经中的盼望是建立在上帝品格和应许上的确信，并非不确定的愿望。提多书2:13把这盼望指向耶稣基督荣耀的显现，使基督复临成为盼望的具体中心。

sampleVerse.text: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;

explanation.en: Rose in the KJV translates a poetic flower name that may refer to a crocus or another blossom rather than the modern garden rose. Song of Solomon 2:1 places the flower beside the lily as an image of beauty in the poem's love dialogue.
explanation.zh: KJV 的 Rose 翻译一个诗歌中的花名，可能指番红花或其他花朵，并不一定是现代园艺中的玫瑰。雅歌2:1把它与百合花并列，在爱情对话中作为美丽的意象。

sampleVerse.text: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.

explanation.en: Incense was a specially blended aromatic substance burned before God in the sanctuary, symbolizing acceptable prayer. Exodus 30:34 names the ingredients of Israel's sacred incense, which was reserved for holy use rather than private imitation.
explanation.zh: 香是用特定配方制成、在圣所中焚烧于上帝面前的芳香物，象征蒙悦纳的祷告。出埃及记30:34列出以色列圣香的材料；这种配方只供圣用，不可私自仿制。

sampleVerse.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight:

explanation.en: To bless is to bestow good, invoke God's favor upon another, or gratefully praise God for his goodness. Numbers 6:24 begins the priestly blessing by asking the LORD himself to bless and keep his people.
explanation.zh: 祝福可以指赐下福益、为别人求上帝眷顾，也可指因上帝良善而称颂祂。民数记6:24以求耶和华亲自赐福并保护百姓，开始祭司的祝福。

sampleVerse.text: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:

explanation.en: Brass in the KJV commonly refers to copper or bronze rather than the later alloy now called brass. Exodus 27:2 commands that the altar and its horns be overlaid with this durable metal for service in the tabernacle court.
explanation.zh: KJV 中的 Brass 通常指铜或青铜，并非后来才出现、现代所称的黄铜。出埃及记27:2吩咐用这种耐用金属包裹祭坛及其四角，供会幕院中的事奉使用。

sampleVerse.text: And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof: his horns shall be of the same: and thou shalt overlay it with brass.

explanation.en: A husband is a man joined to his wife in the covenant of marriage and charged with faithful, self-giving care. Ephesians 5:25 directs husbands to love their wives by the pattern of Christ's sacrificial love for the church.
explanation.zh: 丈夫是在婚姻盟约中与妻子结合的男子，并承担忠诚、舍己照顾的责任。以弗所书5:25吩咐丈夫照基督为教会舍己的爱来爱妻子。

sampleVerse.text: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;

explanation.en: Chosen describes someone or something selected for a purpose by deliberate decision rather than accident. First Peter 2:9 calls believers a chosen generation so that they may proclaim the praises of the One who brought them from darkness into light.
explanation.zh: 蒙拣选表示某人或某物是为特定目的而被有意选定，并非偶然。彼得前书2:9称信徒为蒙拣选的族类，为要宣扬那位召他们出黑暗入光明者的美德。

sampleVerse.text: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:

explanation.en: A feast is a communal meal or appointed festival of remembrance, worship, and rejoicing. Exodus 12:14 establishes Passover as a memorial feast to the LORD, preserving Israel's deliverance from Egypt in the calendar.
explanation.zh: 筵席可以是共同进餐，也可以是为记念、敬拜和欢乐而设立的节期。出埃及记12:14把逾越节定为向耶和华守的记念之节，使出埃及的拯救进入以色列历法。

sampleVerse.text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

explanation.en: Rock denotes solid stone and becomes an image of stability, refuge, and God's faithful provision. First Corinthians 10:4 recalls water supplied in the wilderness and identifies the spiritual Rock accompanying Israel with Christ.
explanation.zh: 磐石指坚固的岩体，也成为稳定、避难和上帝信实供应的象征。哥林多前书10:4回顾旷野中所得的水，并把伴随以色列的属灵磐石认作基督。

sampleVerse.text: And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.

explanation.en: A court is an enclosed open area belonging to a dwelling, palace, prison, tabernacle, or temple. Exodus 27:9 begins the instructions for the tabernacle court, which formed the public outer space around the sacred tent.
explanation.zh: 院子是住宅、宫殿、监狱、会幕或圣殿所属的围合露天空地。出埃及记27:9开始说明会幕院子的建造；它构成圣幕周围供人进入的外部空间。

sampleVerse.text: And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen of an hundred cubits long for one side:

explanation.en: Pieces can mean separate portions of an object and, in the KJV phrase 'pieces of silver,' counted units of payment. Matthew 26:15 records Judas agreeing to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, placing a price on treachery.
explanation.zh: Pieces 可以指一个物体分开的部分；在 KJV 的“银钱”表达中，也指按数计算的付款单位。马太福音26:15记载犹大同意以三十块银钱出卖耶稣，为背叛标上了价格。

sampleVerse.text: And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

explanation.en: Suburbs in the KJV are the pasturelands immediately surrounding a town, not modern residential districts. Numbers 35:2 orders Israel to give the Levites cities to live in together with surrounding land for their livestock.
explanation.zh: KJV 的 Suburbs 指城市四周紧邻的牧场，并非现代住宅郊区。民数记35:2吩咐以色列把城邑给利未人居住，并把周围土地给他们牧养牲畜。

sampleVerse.text: Command the children of Israel, that they give unto the Levites of the inheritance of their possession cities to dwell in; and ye shall give also unto the Levites suburbs for the cities round about them.

explanation.en: Gospel means good news: God's saving work through Jesus Christ, calling people to faith and a renewed life. First Corinthians 15:3 begins Paul's summary with Christ dying for our sins according to the Scriptures, followed by burial and resurrection.
explanation.zh: 福音意为“好消息”，就是上帝借耶稣基督施行拯救，并呼召人信靠祂、过更新的生活。哥林多前书15:3以基督照圣经为我们的罪而死开始保罗的概要，随后还有埋葬与复活。

sampleVerse.text: For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;

explanation.en: Ghost in older KJV English usually means spirit or breath of life, not a wandering apparition. Mark 15:37 says Jesus 'gave up the ghost,' an idiom stating that he truly died on the cross.
explanation.zh: Ghost 在 KJV 古英语中通常指灵或生命气息，并非游荡的幽灵。马可福音15:37说耶稣“交出灵来”，这是说明祂在十字架上真实死亡的旧式表达。

sampleVerse.text: And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.

explanation.en: Prayer is direct communication with God through praise, confession, thanksgiving, lament, intercession, and request. Matthew 6:9 begins Jesus' model prayer with reverence for the heavenly Father and his holy name.
explanation.zh: 祷告是人借赞美、认罪、感恩、哀诉、代求和祈求直接与上帝交流。马太福音6:9以尊崇天父和祂的圣名，开始耶稣所教导的祷告范式。

sampleVerse.text: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

explanation.en: Dust is fine earth and a biblical image of human creatureliness, frailty, mourning, and mortality. Genesis 3:19 says fallen humanity returns to the ground from which it was taken, underscoring that death reverses the gift of life.
explanation.zh: 尘土是细小的土，也在圣经中象征人的受造、脆弱、哀伤和必死。创世记3:19说堕落的人最终归回取他的土地，强调死亡使所赐生命倒转。

sampleVerse.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

explanation.en: Worship is the whole-person response of reverence, loyalty, praise, and service owed to God alone. Revelation 14:7 calls every nation to worship the Creator of heaven, earth, sea, and fountains, echoing creation language also heard in the Sabbath commandment.
explanation.zh: 敬拜是全人以敬畏、忠诚、赞美和事奉回应上帝，而且只归给祂。启示录14:7呼召万民敬拜创造天地海和众水泉源的主，呼应安息日诫命中同样出现的创造语言。

sampleVerse.text: Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.

explanation.en: Bullock is an older term for a young bull or an animal of the cattle kind, often used for sacrifice. First Samuel 1:25 records Hannah's family offering a bullock when bringing the child Samuel to lifelong service at the sanctuary.
explanation.zh: Bullock 是指小公牛或牛类祭牲的旧词。撒母耳记上1:25记载哈拿一家把幼年的撒母耳带到圣所终身事奉时，献上一只公牛。

sampleVerse.text: And they slew a bullock, and brought the child to Eli.

explanation.en: A cloud is condensed moisture in the sky and often serves in Scripture as a veil and sign of God's glorious presence. Exodus 13:21 describes the LORD leading Israel by a pillar of cloud in the daytime during the journey from Egypt.
explanation.zh: 云是天空中凝结的水汽；圣经也常用它遮蔽并标示上帝荣耀的同在。出埃及记13:21描述以色列离开埃及的旅途中，耶和华白日以云柱引领他们。

sampleVerse.text: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

explanation.en: A lamb is a young sheep frequently offered in Israel's sacrifices and central to Passover. John 1:29 calls Jesus the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin, presenting his atoning death as the fulfillment toward which those sacrifices pointed.
explanation.zh: 羔羊是年幼的羊，常用于以色列献祭，也处在逾越节的核心。约翰福音1:29称耶稣为除去世人罪孽的上帝羔羊，表明祂赎罪的死成全了祭牲所指向的意义。

sampleVerse.text: The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

explanation.en: Prince is a ruler or chief who exercises delegated or hereditary authority. Isaiah 9:6 names the promised child Prince of Peace, joining his royal government with the peace his reign establishes.
explanation.zh: 王子或首领是在继承或委任的权柄下治理的人。以赛亚书9:6称应许中的婴孩为“和平的君”，把祂的王权与其统治所建立的和平相连。

sampleVerse.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

explanation.en: Linen is cloth made from flax, valued for coolness and used in ordinary clothing, priestly garments, and sanctuary hangings. Revelation 19:8 interprets the bride's clean fine linen as the righteous deeds of the saints, turning the fabric into a symbol of prepared character.
explanation.zh: 细麻布是由亚麻制成的布料，穿着凉爽，也用于日常衣物、祭司衣袍和圣所帷幕。启示录19:8把新妇洁白的细麻衣解释为圣徒的义行，使这种布成为预备好之品格的象征。

sampleVerse.text: And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints.

explanation.en: Ammon was the nation east of Israel descended from Lot's younger daughter and frequently allied or conflicted with Moab. Judges 11:13 states the Ammonite king's land claim against Israel, which Jephthah answers before the ensuing war.
explanation.zh: 亚扪是以色列东方、源自罗得小女儿后裔的民族，常与摩押结盟或发生冲突。士师记11:13记下亚扪王对以色列提出的领土主张；耶弗他在战争前对此作了回应。

sampleVerse.text: And the king of the children of Ammon answered unto the messengers of Jephthah, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and unto Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably.

explanation.en: Esau was Isaac and Rebekah's firstborn twin, Jacob's brother, and ancestor of Edom. Genesis 25:33 records him selling his birthright to Jacob for immediate food, valuing present appetite above covenant privilege.
explanation.zh: 以扫是以撒和利百加的双胞胎长子、雅各的哥哥，也是以东人的先祖。创世记25:33记载他为眼前食物把长子名分卖给雅各，把即时欲望置于盟约特权之上。

sampleVerse.text: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.

explanation.en: Corn in the KJV normally means cereal grain, especially wheat or barley, not specifically maize. Genesis 42:3 records Joseph's brothers traveling to Egypt to buy grain during famine, a journey that reunites the divided family.
explanation.zh: KJV 的 Corn 通常泛指谷物，尤其是小麦或大麦，并非专指玉米。创世记42:3记载饥荒中约瑟的兄弟下埃及买粮，由此使分裂的家庭重新相遇。

sampleVerse.text: And Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.

explanation.en: Rain determined crops and survival in the biblical land, with early rain preparing soil and latter rain maturing grain. Deuteronomy 11:14 promises both in season so Israel may gather grain, wine, and oil.
explanation.zh: 雨水决定圣经地区的收成和生存；秋雨预备土壤，春雨使谷物成熟。申命记11:14应许按时赐下这两种雨，使以色列可以收取五谷、新酒和油。

sampleVerse.text: That I will give you the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil.

explanation.en: A curse is a solemn pronouncement of judgment or calamity, the opposite of blessing. Galatians 3:13 says Christ redeemed humanity from the law's curse by bearing its condemnation on the cross, opening a life shaped by grace and faithful obedience.
explanation.zh: 咒诅是严肃宣告审判或灾祸，与祝福相反。加拉太书3:13说基督在十字架上承担定罪，使人脱离律法的咒诅，并开启由恩典和忠心顺服塑造的生命。

sampleVerse.text: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:

explanation.en: Iron is a strong metal used for tools, weapons, fittings, and restraints in the biblical world. Deuteronomy 8:9 describes the promised land as containing iron in its stones, adding mineral resources to its agricultural abundance.
explanation.zh: 铁是坚硬金属，在圣经时代用于工具、武器、构件和锁链。申命记8:9说应许之地的石头中有铁，把矿产资源也列入那地的丰富供应。

sampleVerse.text: A land wherein thou shalt eat bread without scarceness, thou shalt not lack any thing in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills thou mayest dig brass.

explanation.en: A plague is a severe disease, blow, or widespread calamity; the Exodus plagues exposed Egypt's resistance to God. Exodus 9:14 warns Pharaoh that intensified judgments would make him know there is none like the LORD in all the earth.
explanation.zh: 灾祸可以指严重疾病、打击或广泛灾难；出埃及的诸灾显露埃及对上帝的抗拒。出埃及记9:14警告法老，更重的审判要使他知道全地没有像耶和华的。

sampleVerse.text: For I will at this time send all my plagues upon thine heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people; that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.

explanation.en: A tent is a portable fabric dwelling suited to shepherds, travelers, and nomadic life. Hebrews 11:9 recalls Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob living in tents in the promised land, confessing that they still awaited God's lasting city.
explanation.zh: 帐棚是可移动的布质住所，适合牧人、旅客和游牧生活。希伯来书11:9回顾亚伯拉罕、以撒和雅各在应许之地住帐棚，表明他们仍等候上帝所建的永恒之城。

sampleVerse.text: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

explanation.en: Famine is an extreme scarcity of food caused by failed harvests, war, siege, or other disaster. Genesis 41:30 foretells seven years of Egyptian famine after abundance, the crisis through which Joseph would preserve many lives.
explanation.zh: 饥荒是因歉收、战争、围城或其他灾难造成的严重粮食短缺。创世记41:30预告埃及七个丰年后将有七个荒年；约瑟正借这场危机保全许多人的性命。

sampleVerse.text: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;

explanation.en: Hour may mean a measured part of the day or an appointed moment of special significance. Mark 15:25 places Jesus' crucifixion at the third hour, anchoring the central saving event in historical time.
explanation.zh: 时辰可以指一天中计算的时段，也可指具有特殊意义的指定时刻。马可福音15:25把耶稣被钉十字架定在第三时辰，使救恩的核心事件落在具体历史时间中。

sampleVerse.text: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

explanation.en: A prison confines people under legal or political authority and in Scripture often becomes a setting of injustice as well as deliverance. Genesis 39:20 records innocent Joseph imprisoned through a false accusation, before God raised him to govern Egypt.
explanation.zh: 监狱是在法律或政治权力下拘禁人的地方；圣经中它常是不义发生之处，也成为拯救展开的背景。创世记39:20记载无辜的约瑟因诬告入狱，后来上帝却使他升任埃及治理者。

sampleVerse.text: And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.

explanation.en: Simon was a common Jewish name, most famously borne by the fisherman whom Jesus renamed Peter. Mark 1:16 introduces Simon casting a net with his brother Andrew immediately before Jesus calls them to follow him.
explanation.zh: 西门是常见的犹太名字，其中最著名的是后来被耶稣改名彼得的渔夫。马可福音1:16介绍西门与兄弟安得烈撒网，紧接着耶稣便呼召他们跟从祂。

sampleVerse.text: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.

explanation.en: To fast is voluntarily to abstain from food for a time in order to seek God with focused prayer, grief, or repentance. Matthew 6:17 tells the fasting disciple to maintain ordinary appearance, rejecting performance for human praise.
explanation.zh: 禁食是人在一段时间内自愿不进食，以专心祷告、哀伤或悔改寻求上帝。马太福音6:17吩咐禁食的门徒保持平常外表，拒绝以宗教表演换取人的称赞。

sampleVerse.text: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;

explanation.en: An army is an organized body of soldiers arranged under commanders for war. First Samuel 17:21 depicts Israel and the Philistines setting their forces in battle array just before David hears Goliath's challenge.
explanation.zh: 军队是按指挥体系组织起来、用于作战的士兵群体。撒母耳记上17:21描写以色列和非利士双方摆列队伍，随后大卫便听见歌利亚的挑战。

sampleVerse.text: For Israel and the Philistines had put the battle in array, army against army.

explanation.en: Blind describes inability to see and is also used figuratively for failure to perceive spiritual truth. John 9:1 introduces a man blind from birth whose healing becomes a sign of Jesus' work and exposes the chosen blindness of his critics.
explanation.zh: 瞎眼指不能看见，也可比喻人无法辨认属灵真理。约翰福音9:1介绍一个生来瞎眼的人；他的医治成为耶稣工作的记号，也揭露批评者自选的属灵盲目。

sampleVerse.text: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.

explanation.en: A plain is broad, relatively level land, often suited to travel, settlement, or cultivation. Genesis 13:10 describes the well-watered Jordan plain that attracted Lot, though its prosperous appearance concealed Sodom's danger.
explanation.zh: 平原是广阔而相对平坦的土地，常适合通行、定居或耕作。创世记13:10描写水源充足、吸引罗得的约旦平原；然而繁荣外表遮盖了所多玛的危险。

sampleVerse.text: And Lot lifted up his eyes, and beheld all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered every where, before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, even as the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as thou comest unto Zoar.

explanation.en: Amen is a Hebrew affirmation meaning truly, certainly, or let it be so, used to confirm prayer and promise. Revelation 22:20 answers Christ's promise to come quickly with 'Amen' and an appeal for his coming.
explanation.zh: 阿们是希伯来语的肯定词，意为“诚然”“确实”或“愿如此成就”，用于确认祷告和应许。启示录22:20以“阿们”和求主降临的呼声，回应基督必快来的应许。

sampleVerse.text: He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

explanation.en: The church is the community called and gathered by God through Christ, not merely a building or institution. Acts 2:47 describes the Lord adding saved people to this fellowship, showing that its growth comes through God's saving work.
explanation.zh: 教会是上帝借基督呼召并聚集的群体，并不只是建筑或机构。使徒行传2:47描述主把得救的人天天加给这个团契，显明教会增长来自上帝的拯救工作。

sampleVerse.text: Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.

explanation.en: A hill is a rounded rise of land smaller than a mountain and often served as a visible site for towns or worship. Matthew 5:14 compares Jesus' disciples to a city set on a hill whose light cannot be hidden.
explanation.zh: 山冈是比山较小、顶部较圆的高地，常成为显眼的城镇或敬拜地点。马太福音5:14把耶稣的门徒比作建在山上的城，其光无法隐藏。

sampleVerse.text: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.

explanation.en: Selah is a musical or liturgical notation appearing mainly in Psalms, though its precise meaning remains uncertain. Psalm 3:2 places it after the enemies' claim that David has no help in God, likely marking a pause before his confident reply.
explanation.zh: 细拉是主要出现在诗篇中的音乐或礼仪记号，确切含义仍不能确定。诗篇3:2把它放在仇敌声称大卫不得上帝帮助之后，可能标示停顿，随后转入他的信心回应。

sampleVerse.text: Many there be which say of my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.

explanation.en: White is a color associated in Scripture with light, purity, victory, and cleansed garments. Isaiah 1:18 promises that sins red like scarlet can become white as snow through God's gracious cleansing.
explanation.zh: 白色在圣经中与光明、纯洁、得胜和洗净的衣袍相连。以赛亚书1:18应许，虽罪如朱红，也能因上帝恩慈的洁净变得白如雪。

sampleVerse.text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

explanation.en: A dream is an experience of images and thoughts during sleep, sometimes used by God in Scripture to reveal a purpose. Genesis 37:5 introduces Joseph's dream of future elevation, which provoked his brothers and began the path toward its surprising fulfillment.
explanation.zh: 梦是睡眠中出现的图像和思想；圣经记载上帝有时借梦启示旨意。创世记37:5介绍约瑟关于将来升高的梦；它激怒兄弟，也开启了出人意料的应验过程。

sampleVerse.text: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.

explanation.en: Levi was Jacob and Leah's third son and ancestor of the priestly tribe set apart for sanctuary service. Genesis 29:34 connects his name with Leah's hope that her husband would now be joined to her after a third son.
explanation.zh: 利未是雅各和利亚的第三个儿子，也是后来分别出来从事圣所事奉之支派的先祖。创世记29:34把他的名字与利亚的盼望相连：生了第三个儿子后，丈夫会与她联合。

sampleVerse.text: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.

explanation.en: Doors control entrance to houses, cities, courts, and sacred spaces and can symbolize welcome or exclusion. Psalm 24:7 poetically commands ancient doors to lift up for the King of glory, portraying God's triumphant entrance.
explanation.zh: 门控制住宅、城市、院落和圣所的出入，也可象征接纳或拒绝。诗篇24:7以诗歌语言吩咐永久的门户抬起，让荣耀的王得胜进入。

sampleVerse.text: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.

explanation.en: Fury is fierce, overflowing anger that threatens destructive action. Genesis 27:44 describes Esau's rage after Jacob took the blessing, prompting Jacob to remain away until that fury subsided.
explanation.zh: 暴怒是猛烈而泛滥、可能引发毁坏行动的怒气。创世记27:44描述雅各夺得祝福后以扫的怒火，因此雅各必须离开，等这怒气消退。

sampleVerse.text: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away;

explanation.en: A burden may be a physical load, a heavy responsibility, or an oracle whose grave message weighs upon a prophet. Habakkuk 1:1 calls the prophet's vision a burden, introducing his struggle with violence, justice, and God's answer.
explanation.zh: 重担可以是身体所负的重量、沉重责任，也可指压在先知心上的严肃默示。哈巴谷书1:1称先知所见的异象为默示或重担，由此引出他对暴力、公义和上帝回答的追问。

sampleVerse.text: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.

explanation.en: A measure is a standard amount or the act of determining quantity, and it can symbolize the standard used toward others. Luke 6:38 warns that the measure people use will be used toward them, joining generosity with moral accountability.
explanation.zh: 量器是规定的容量，也可指衡量数量的行为；它还能象征人对待别人的尺度。路加福音6:38警告人用什么量器量给别人，也必用什么量器量给自己，把慷慨与道德责任相连。

sampleVerse.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

explanation.en: A grave is a burial place where the dead body is laid to rest while awaiting resurrection. John 11:17 says Lazarus had been in the grave four days before Jesus raised him, demonstrating Christ's authority to awaken the dead.
explanation.zh: 坟墓是安放死者身体、等候复活的地方。约翰福音11:17说拉撒路已在坟墓里四天，随后耶稣使他复活，显明基督唤醒死者的权柄。

sampleVerse.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.

explanation.en: Scribes were trained readers, copyists, and teachers of the law, influential in Jewish religious and legal life. Matthew 23:2 recognizes their teaching seat with the Pharisees, before Jesus condemns the gap between their instruction and conduct.
explanation.zh: 文士是受过训练的律法阅读者、抄写者和教师，在犹太宗教与法律生活中很有影响。马太福音23:2承认他们与法利赛人坐在摩西的位上，随后耶稣责备其教导与行为不一致。

sampleVerse.text: Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat:

explanation.en: Bethel means house of God and was a central hill-country town that later became both a worship site and a center of corrupt worship. Genesis 28:19 records Jacob renaming Luz after his dream of God's presence and promise there.
explanation.zh: 伯特利意为“上帝的殿”，是中部山地的重要城市，后来既是敬拜地点，也成为败坏崇拜的中心。创世记28:19记载雅各在那里梦见上帝的同在与应许后，把路斯改名为伯特利。

sampleVerse.text: And he called the name of that place Beth-el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.

explanation.en: A crown signifies royal authority, honor, victory, or a reward bestowed after faithful endurance. Second Timothy 4:8 looks forward to the crown of righteousness Christ will give at his appearing, grounding reward in the righteous Judge's promise.
explanation.zh: 冠冕象征王权、尊荣、得胜，或忠心忍耐后所得的赏赐。提摩太后书4:8盼望基督显现时赐下公义的冠冕，把赏赐建立在公义审判者的应许上。

sampleVerse.text: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.

explanation.en: Rent in older KJV English can be the past tense of rend, meaning torn, rather than payment for property. Mark 15:38 says the temple veil was rent from top to bottom when Jesus died, signaling a decisive change in access to God.
explanation.zh: Rent 在 KJV 古英语中可以是 rend 的过去式，意思是“撕裂”，而不是房租。马可福音15:38说耶稣死时圣殿幔子从上到下裂开，标志人来到上帝面前的途径发生决定性改变。

sampleVerse.text: And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

explanation.en: The deep denotes a vast depth of water, an abyss, or the sea beyond ordinary human reach. Genesis 1:2 pictures darkness over the face of the deep before God orders and fills the unformed creation.
explanation.zh: 深渊指广大深水、无底处，或人力难以到达的海洋深处。创世记1:2描写上帝整理并充满尚未成形的世界以前，黑暗笼罩渊面。

sampleVerse.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

explanation.en: A chariot was a fast wheeled vehicle used especially by kings and armies, giving trained forces a battlefield advantage. Exodus 14:6 records Pharaoh preparing his chariot to pursue Israel, whose escape would show that such power could not defeat God.
explanation.zh: 战车是快速的轮式车辆，尤其用于君王出行和军队作战，使受训部队取得战场优势。出埃及记14:6记载法老预备战车追赶以色列；随后的脱逃显明这种力量不能胜过上帝。

sampleVerse.text: And he made ready his chariot, and took his people with him:

explanation.en: Hair can mark identity, age, mourning, beauty, or a special vow, as in the Nazirite practice. Luke 21:18 uses the safety of every hair as a vivid promise that no loss can finally escape God's knowledge and care.
explanation.zh: 头发在圣经中可标示身份、年龄、哀悼、美丽或特殊誓愿，例如拿细耳人的做法。路加福音21:18以连一根头发也不损坏的形象，保证任何损失最终都不会脱离上帝的知晓与保守。

sampleVerse.text: But there shall not an hair of your head perish.

explanation.en: A blemish is a defect that disqualified an animal from being offered as a complete sacrifice. First Peter 1:19 calls Christ a lamb without blemish and spot, presenting his sinless life and atoning death as the perfect ransom.
explanation.zh: 瑕疵是会使祭牲不符合完整献祭要求的缺陷。彼得前书1:19称基督为无瑕疵、无玷污的羔羊，表明祂无罪的生命和赎罪之死是完全的赎价。

sampleVerse.text: But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot:

explanation.en: Grass was common pasture but withered quickly under the dry land's heat, making it a picture of mortal brevity. Isaiah 40:6 compares all flesh and its glory to grass and flowers, before contrasting them with God's enduring word.
explanation.zh: 草是常见的牧草，却在干旱地区的热风下迅速枯萎，因此成为人生短暂的图像。以赛亚书40:6把凡有血气者及其荣美比作草和花，随后与上帝长存的话形成对比。

sampleVerse.text: The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:

explanation.en: The neck supports the head and in biblical imagery can express submission, bondage, or stubborn pride. Psalm 75:5 warns the arrogant not to lift the horn high or speak with a stiff neck against God.
explanation.zh: 颈项支撑头部，在圣经意象中可表示顺服、奴役或顽梗骄傲。诗篇75:5警告狂傲的人不要高举角，也不可挺着颈项说话敌对上帝。

sampleVerse.text: Lift not up your horn on high: speak not with a stiff neck.

explanation.en: The grapevine was a major biblical crop and a frequent image for Israel, fruitfulness, and covenant responsibility. John 15:1 identifies Jesus as the true vine and the Father as the husbandman, making dependent union with Christ the source of fruit.
explanation.zh: 葡萄树是圣经地区的重要作物，也常象征以色列、结果和盟约责任。约翰福音15:1称耶稣为真葡萄树、父为栽培的人，说明与基督保持倚赖的联合才是结果的源头。

sampleVerse.text: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.

explanation.en: Devil means slanderer and names the same adversary also called Satan, the serpent, and the deceiver. Revelation 12:9 gathers these titles together and describes his worldwide deception before God's victory removes him.
explanation.zh: 魔鬼意为“毁谤者”，与撒但、古蛇和迷惑者都是同一仇敌的称呼。启示录12:9把这些称号集中起来，描述他迷惑普天下，也宣告上帝最终将他除去。

sampleVerse.text: And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.

explanation.en: Harvest is the season when mature crops are gathered and often symbolizes judgment or people ready to receive the gospel. Matthew 9:37 says the harvest is plentiful but workers are few, leading Jesus to call for prayer and mission.
explanation.zh: 收割是成熟庄稼被收聚的季节，也常象征审判，或已经预备接受福音的人群。马太福音9:37说庄稼多、工人少，因此耶稣呼召人祷告并参与使命。

sampleVerse.text: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;

explanation.en: An oath solemnly confirms a statement or promise by appealing to a greater authority as witness. Hebrews 6:13 says God swore by himself when promising Abraham because no greater authority existed, assuring the certainty of his word.
explanation.zh: 誓言是诉诸更高权威作见证，严肃确认陈述或应许。希伯来书6:13说上帝向亚伯拉罕应许时，因没有比自己更大的，就指着自己起誓，保证祂话语的可靠。

sampleVerse.text: For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,

explanation.en: Evening is the period around and after sunset and in biblical reckoning commonly begins a new day. Genesis 1:5 joins evening and morning as the first day, providing the creation pattern behind sunset-to-sunset Sabbath observance.
explanation.zh: 晚上是日落前后的时段；按圣经计日方式，它通常开始新的一天。创世记1:5把晚上和早晨合为第一日，构成安息日从日落到日落遵守的创造模式。

sampleVerse.text: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.

explanation.en: A journey is travel from one place to another, often carrying a person through testing, change, and dependence. Exodus 13:21 says God guided Israel's journey from Egypt with cloud by day and fire by night.
explanation.zh: 旅程是从一处前往另一处的过程，常使人经历考验、改变和倚靠。出埃及记13:21说上帝在以色列离开埃及的旅途中，白日以云柱、夜间以火柱引导。

sampleVerse.text: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

explanation.en: A captive is someone held under the power of a conqueror, prison, debt, or other bondage. Luke 4:18 announces liberty to captives as part of Jesus' Spirit-anointed mission, joining physical and spiritual release under God's saving reign.
explanation.zh: 被掳者是受征服者、监狱、债务或其他捆绑权势控制的人。路加福音4:18把释放被掳者列入耶稣受圣灵膏抹的使命，使身体和属灵的释放同归于上帝的救恩统治。

sampleVerse.text: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,

explanation.en: A gift is something freely given rather than earned, whether material help, ability, office, or divine grace. James 1:17 traces every good and perfect gift to the unchanging Father of lights.
explanation.zh: 礼物是白白赐下而非赚取的事物，可以是物质帮助、能力、职分或神圣恩典。雅各书1:17把各样美善和全备的恩赐追溯到永不改变的众光之父。

sampleVerse.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

explanation.en: A yoke joins draft animals for work and figuratively represents service, discipline, or oppressive bondage. Matthew 11:29 invites disciples to take Jesus' yoke and learn from his meekness, finding rest in willing submission to him.
explanation.zh: 轭把役畜连在一起工作，比喻事奉、管教或压迫性的捆绑。马太福音11:29邀请门徒负耶稣的轭，学习祂的柔和，在甘心顺服中得到安息。

sampleVerse.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

explanation.en: Flour is grain ground into meal for daily bread and for several sanctuary offerings. Leviticus 24:5 commands fine flour to be baked into twelve loaves of showbread, representing Israel continually before God.
explanation.zh: 面粉是谷物磨成的粉，用于日常制饼和多种圣所供物。利未记24:5吩咐用细面烤成十二个陈设饼，代表以色列常在上帝面前。

sampleVerse.text: And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof: two tenth deals shall be in one cake.

explanation.en: Shimei son of Gera was a Benjaminite of Saul's house who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion. Second Samuel 16:5 records him coming from Bahurim and cursing as the fleeing king approached, testing David's restraint.
explanation.zh: 基拉的儿子示每是扫罗家族的便雅悯人，在押沙龙叛乱期间咒骂大卫。撒母耳记下16:5记载逃亡的王接近巴户琳时，他出来咒骂，考验了大卫的克制。

sampleVerse.text: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.

explanation.en: Honey was gathered from wild bees or produced from fruit syrup and symbolized the land's abundance and sweetness. First Samuel 14:27 records Jonathan being refreshed by wild honey, unaware of Saul's rash ban on food.
explanation.zh: 蜜可来自野蜂，也可指浓缩果浆，在圣经中象征土地的丰盛与甘甜。撒母耳记上14:27记载约拿单吃野蜜后精神恢复，却不知道扫罗曾草率禁止百姓进食。

sampleVerse.text: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.

explanation.en: Tables in older KJV English can mean flat tablets for writing, not only furniture used for meals. Exodus 31:18 calls the two stone tablets of testimony 'tables,' inscribed by God's finger with the covenant law.
explanation.zh: Tables 在 KJV 古英语中可指用于书写的平板，不只指吃饭的桌子。出埃及记31:18把两块法版称为“石版”，上面由上帝的指头写下盟约律法。

sampleVerse.text: And he gave unto Moses, when he had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God.

explanation.en: Food sustains created life and is received as a gift that should be used with gratitude, wisdom, and self-control. Genesis 1:29 gives humanity seed-bearing plants and fruit for food, presenting the original creation diet as plant-based.
explanation.zh: 食物维持受造生命，是应当以感恩、智慧和节制领受的礼物。创世记1:29把结种子的植物和果子赐给人作食物，显示起初创造中的饮食以植物为本。

sampleVerse.text: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.

explanation.en: Sinai is the mountain and wilderness region where Israel camped after the Exodus and entered covenant with God. Exodus 19:20 records the LORD descending on the summit and calling Moses upward before giving the Ten Commandments.
explanation.zh: 西奈是以色列出埃及后扎营、并与上帝立约的山与旷野地区。出埃及记19:20记载耶和华降临山顶，召摩西上去，随后赐下十诫。

sampleVerse.text: And the LORD came down upon mount Sinai, on the top of the mount: and the LORD called Moses up to the top of the mount; and Moses went up.

explanation.en: Azariah was the Hebrew name of Daniel's companion whom the Babylonian official renamed Abednego. Daniel 1:7 records the imposed names, part of an attempt to reshape the exiles' identity even as they remained faithful to God.
explanation.zh: 亚撒利雅是但以理同伴的希伯来名字；巴比伦官员把他改名为亚伯尼歌。但以理书1:7记下这些强加的名字，显示帝国试图重塑被掳者身份，而他们仍忠于上帝。

sampleVerse.text: Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave unto Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abed-nego.

explanation.en: Beyond means on the farther side of a boundary, so its location changes with the speaker's viewpoint. Joshua 1:14 uses it for the land across the Jordan already given to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh while their warriors crossed west to help Israel.
explanation.zh: 彼岸是指某道边界的另一边，因此位置会随说话者视角改变。约书亚记1:14用它指流便、迦得和玛拿西半支派在约旦河另一边所得之地，而他们的战士仍要过河帮助以色列。

sampleVerse.text: Your wives, your little ones, and your cattle, shall remain in the land which Moses gave you on this side Jordan; but ye shall pass before your brethren armed, all the mighty men of valour, and help them;

explanation.en: Hell in the KJV translates several different terms, including the grave and the final place of judgment, so context must decide its meaning. Revelation 20:14 says death and hell are cast into the lake of fire, calls this the second death, and portrays the final defeat of death and evil.
explanation.zh: KJV 的 Hell 翻译数个不同词语，包括坟墓和最终审判之处，因此必须按上下文判断。启示录20:14说死亡和阴间被扔进火湖，称这为第二次的死，并描绘死亡与罪恶最终被击败。

sampleVerse.text: And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.

explanation.en: Mary of Nazareth was the mother of Jesus, a Jewish woman who received an extraordinary calling with trust. Luke 1:38 records her willing submission to God's word after Gabriel announced the virgin conception.
explanation.zh: 拿撒勒的马利亚是耶稣的母亲，是一位以信靠领受非凡呼召的犹太女子。路加福音1:38记载加百列宣告童女怀孕后，她甘愿顺服上帝的话。

sampleVerse.text: And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.

explanation.en: A queen may be a woman who rules or the wife of a king, with influence varying by kingdom and period. Esther 2:17 records Ahasuerus placing the royal crown on Esther and making her queen instead of Vashti.
explanation.zh: 王后可以是亲自治理的女性君王，也可指国王的妻子，其权力随国家和时代而不同。以斯帖记2:17记载亚哈随鲁把王冠戴在以斯帖头上，立她代替瓦实提为后。

sampleVerse.text: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.

explanation.en: The ephod was a distinctive priestly garment, especially associated with Israel's high priest, made with skilled weaving and precious materials. Exodus 28:6 specifies gold and colored yarn for its construction as part of the sanctuary vestments.
explanation.zh: 以弗得是独特的祭司衣袍，尤其与以色列大祭司有关，以精巧织工和珍贵材料制成。出埃及记28:6规定用金线和彩色线制作，作为圣所礼服的一部分。

sampleVerse.text: And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and of purple, of scarlet, and fine twined linen, with cunning work.

explanation.en: Ramah was a Benjaminite hill-town and the home of Elkanah, Hannah, and their son Samuel. First Samuel 1:19 records the family returning there after worship at Shiloh, just before God answers Hannah's prayer for a child.
explanation.zh: 拉玛是便雅悯境内的山城，也是以利加拿、哈拿和儿子撒母耳的家乡。撒母耳记上1:19记载一家人在示罗敬拜后回到那里，紧接着上帝便回应哈拿求子的祷告。

sampleVerse.text: And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the LORD, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.

explanation.en: A chamber is a private room, often an upper room used for lodging, prayer, storage, or gathering. Acts 20:8 locates the Troas believers in a lamp-filled upper chamber before Eutychus falls and is restored to life.
explanation.zh: 内室是较私密的房间，常位于楼上，用于住宿、祷告、储物或聚会。使徒行传20:8把特罗亚信徒的聚会放在点着许多灯的楼上内室，随后发生犹推古坠楼并复生的事件。

sampleVerse.text: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

explanation.en: Scarlet is a vivid red dye used in rich clothing, sanctuary fabric, and images of bloodguilt. Isaiah 1:18 compares deeply stained sins to scarlet and crimson, then promises cleansing white as snow and wool.
explanation.zh: 朱红是鲜艳的红色染料，用于华贵衣物、圣所织物，也象征流血之罪。以赛亚书1:18把深重的罪比作朱红和丹颜，又应许把它洁净得白如雪和羊毛。

sampleVerse.text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

explanation.en: Cedar is a tall, fragrant, durable tree whose timber from Lebanon was prized for palaces and the temple. First Kings 5:10 records Hiram supplying Solomon with cedar and fir according to their agreement.
explanation.zh: 香柏是高大、芳香而耐久的树；黎巴嫩香柏木尤其用于宫殿和圣殿。列王纪上5:10记载希兰按约供应所罗门香柏木和松木。

sampleVerse.text: So Hiram gave Solomon cedar trees and fir trees according to all his desire.

explanation.en: To guard is to watch and protect against danger; a guard is the person or force assigned to that duty. Nehemiah 4:9 joins prayer to God with setting a watch against attackers, showing faithful dependence expressed through prudent action.
explanation.zh: 守卫就是警醒并保护人免受危险；守卫者则是承担这责任的人或队伍。尼希米记4:9把向上帝祷告与设立防备敌人的守望结合，显示信靠也要借审慎行动表达。

sampleVerse.text: Nevertheless we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night, because of them.

explanation.en: The moon is the lesser light appointed to govern the night and help mark seasons and months. Genesis 1:16 presents it as a created light rather than a deity, placing it under the Creator's rule.
explanation.zh: 月亮是被指定管理夜晚、并帮助标记节令和月份的较小光体。创世记1:16把它描写为受造之光，而非神明，使它处于创造主权下。

sampleVerse.text: And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.

explanation.en: Stars are distant lights in the heavens used to mark times and often symbolize an innumerable multitude. Genesis 15:5 asks Abraham to count them and makes their number an image of the descendants God promised him.
explanation.zh: 星辰是天空中遥远的光体，用来标记时令，也常象征无法数算的众多。创世记15:5请亚伯拉罕数星，并以其数量比喻上帝应许给他的后裔。

sampleVerse.text: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.

explanation.en: Wheat was a major grain crop ground for bread and harvested by threshing and winnowing. Matthew 13:25 places an enemy's tares among the wheat, beginning Jesus' parable about good and evil growing together until judgment.
explanation.zh: 小麦是重要谷物，磨粉制饼，并经过打谷和簸扬收获。马太福音13:25写仇敌把稗子撒在麦子中间，由此开始耶稣关于善恶一同生长直到审判的比喻。

sampleVerse.text: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.

explanation.en: Blue dye was used with purple and scarlet in Israel's sanctuary textiles and priestly garments. Exodus 28:31 requires the high priest's robe of the ephod to be entirely blue, giving the sacred clothing a distinctive appearance.
explanation.zh: 蓝色染料与紫色、朱红色一同用于以色列圣所织物和祭司衣袍。出埃及记28:31规定大祭司以弗得的外袍要全是蓝色，使圣服具有独特外观。

sampleVerse.text: And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.

explanation.en: Micah of Moresheth was a prophet to Judah who denounced exploitation and announced both judgment and restoration. Micah 1:1 dates his message across the reigns of three kings and identifies his visions concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
explanation.zh: 摩利沙人弥迦是向犹大传道的先知，谴责剥削，也宣告审判与复兴。弥迦书1:1把他的信息定在三位君王时期，并说明异象涉及撒玛利亚和耶路撒冷。

sampleVerse.text: The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

explanation.en: Sheba was a wealthy South Arabian kingdom associated with long-distance trade in spices and gold. First Kings 10:1 records its queen traveling to test Solomon's famed wisdom with difficult questions.
explanation.zh: 示巴是富有的南阿拉伯王国，与香料和黄金的远途贸易有关。列王纪上10:1记载示巴女王远道而来，用难题考问声名远播的所罗门智慧。

sampleVerse.text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to prove him with hard questions.

explanation.en: Joram, also called Jehoram, was Ahab's son and king of northern Israel after Ahaziah. Second Kings 3:1 dates his accession during Jehoshaphat's reign in Judah, introducing the ruler involved in the campaign against Moab.
explanation.zh: 约兰又称约兰，是亚哈的儿子，在亚哈谢之后作北国以色列王。列王纪下3:1把他的登基定在犹大王约沙法年间，并引出后来攻打摩押的统治者。

sampleVerse.text: Now Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned twelve years.

explanation.en: Cyrus was the Persian conqueror of Babylon whose policy allowed displaced peoples, including the Jews, to restore their sanctuaries. Ezra 1:1 records the LORD stirring him to issue the decree for Jerusalem's temple to be rebuilt.
explanation.zh: 古列是征服巴比伦的波斯王；他的政策准许包括犹太人在内的被迁民族重建圣所。以斯拉记1:1记载耶和华激动他的心，颁令重建耶路撒冷圣殿。

sampleVerse.text: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,

explanation.en: Elam was a son of Shem and the name of the people and highland country east of Babylonia associated with his descendants. Genesis 10:22 places him in Shem's family line, giving the biblical genealogy behind the national name.
explanation.zh: 以拦是闪的儿子，也成为巴比伦以东高地及其民族的名称，与他的后裔相连。创世记10:22把他列在闪的家谱中，给出这个民族名称的圣经谱系背景。

sampleVerse.text: The children of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.

explanation.en: Johanan son of Kareah was a Judean military leader after Jerusalem fell, who warned of Ishmael's plot but later resisted Jeremiah's counsel. Jeremiah 42:1 shows him and other leaders asking the prophet to pray for the remnant before they chose Egypt.
explanation.zh: 加利亚的儿子约哈难是耶路撒冷陷落后的犹大将领；他曾警告以实玛利的阴谋，后来却抗拒耶利米的劝告。耶利米书42:1记载他与众首领在选择去埃及前，请先知为余民祷告。

sampleVerse.text: Then all the captains of the forces, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least even unto the greatest, came near,

explanation.en: Darius is the royal name of several rulers; Daniel's Darius the Mede governed Babylon after its fall. Daniel 6:9 records him signing the prayer ban that officials designed to trap Daniel, a decree the king soon regretted.
explanation.zh: 大利乌是多位君王使用的王名；但以理书中的玛代人大利乌在巴比伦陷落后治理当地。但以理书6:9记载他签署官员为陷害但以理而设计的禁令，随后很快后悔。

sampleVerse.text: Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

explanation.en: Ashdod was a chief Philistine coastal city and a center of the worship of Dagon. First Samuel 5:2 records the Philistines placing Israel's captured ark in Dagon's temple, where the idol's fall exposed their false triumph.
explanation.zh: 亚实突是非利士主要沿海城市，也是大衮崇拜中心。撒母耳记上5:2记载非利士人把掳来的约柜放进大衮庙；随后偶像倒下，显出他们的胜利是假象。

sampleVerse.text: When the Philistines took the ark of God, they brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon.

explanation.en: Nabal was a wealthy Calebite whose name means fool and whose harshness endangered his household. First Samuel 25:3 contrasts his churlish character with the wisdom of his wife Abigail, preparing for her intervention with David.
explanation.zh: 拿八是富有的迦勒族人，名字意为“愚顽”；他的粗暴使全家陷入危险。撒母耳记上25:3把他的乖僻与妻子亚比该的聪慧对照，为她后来出面劝阻大卫铺路。

sampleVerse.text: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.

explanation.en: Naboth was a Jezreelite who owned an ancestral vineyard beside Ahab's palace. First Kings 21:3 records him refusing to surrender the inheritance God had entrusted to his family, leading Jezebel to arrange his judicial murder.
explanation.zh: 拿伯是耶斯列人，在亚哈王宫旁拥有祖传葡萄园。列王纪上21:3记载他拒绝交出上帝托付给家族的产业，结果耶洗别策划以司法手段杀害他。

sampleVerse.text: And Naboth said to Ahab, The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

explanation.en: Asia in the New Testament usually means the Roman province in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus as its chief city, not the modern continent. Acts 19:10 says people throughout that province heard the Lord's word during Paul's extended ministry.
explanation.zh: 新约中的亚细亚通常指小亚细亚西部、以以弗所为首府的罗马行省，并非现代的亚洲大陆。使徒行传19:10说保罗长期事奉期间，全省的人都听见了主的道。

sampleVerse.text: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

explanation.en: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah and married into Ahab's idolatrous dynasty. Second Chronicles 21:4 records him killing his brothers after securing the throne, revealing the violent apostasy that marked his reign.
explanation.zh: 约沙法的儿子约兰作犹大王，并与亚哈拜偶像的王朝联姻。历代志下21:4记载他巩固王位后杀死众兄弟，显出其统治中的暴力与背道。

sampleVerse.text: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Israel.

explanation.en: Machir was Manasseh's son and ancestor of a clan known for taking territory in Gilead. Numbers 32:40 records Moses giving Gilead to Machir's descendants after they captured it.
explanation.zh: 玛吉是玛拿西的儿子，也是以攻取基列地区闻名之宗族的先祖。民数记32:40记载玛吉的后裔夺取那地后，摩西把基列赐给他们。

sampleVerse.text: And Moses gave Gilead unto Machir the son of Manasseh; and he dwelt therein.

explanation.en: Gaza was an ancient coastal stronghold and one of the five chief Philistine cities, controlling trade routes toward Egypt. Amos 1:7 announces fire against its wall after the city participated in carrying whole communities into slavery.
explanation.zh: 迦萨是古老的沿海坚城，也是非利士五座主要城市之一，控制通往埃及的商路。阿摩司书1:7因这城参与把整批人口卖为奴隶，宣告火要烧毁其城墙。

sampleVerse.text: But I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, which shall devour the palaces thereof:

explanation.en: The Arnon is a river gorge flowing west into the Dead Sea and forming a major boundary east of Jordan. Deuteronomy 3:16 uses its middle and banks to mark territory given to Reuben and Gad beside Moab and Ammon.
explanation.zh: 亚嫩河穿过峡谷向西流入死海，是约旦河东的重要边界。申命记3:16以河中和河岸标示分给流便、迦得并邻近摩押、亚扪的土地。

sampleVerse.text: And unto the Reubenites and unto the Gadites I gave from Gilead even unto the river Arnon half the valley, and the border even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;

explanation.en: Jeshua son of Jozadak was the high priest who returned from Babylon and worked with Zerubbabel to restore worship. Ezra 3:2 records him helping rebuild the altar and resume offerings according to the law of Moses.
explanation.zh: 约萨达的儿子耶书亚是从巴比伦归回的大祭司，与所罗巴伯一同恢复敬拜。以斯拉记3:2记载他协助重建祭坛，并照摩西律法重新献祭。

sampleVerse.text: Then stood up Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and builded the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings thereon, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.

explanation.en: Tamar was Judah's widowed daughter-in-law, denied the family protection and offspring she had been promised. Genesis 38:26 records Judah acknowledging that she was more righteous than he, exposing his failure of duty after her risky deception.
explanation.zh: 她玛是犹大的寡居儿媳，却没有得到家族所应许的保护和后裔。创世记38:26记载犹大在她冒险设局后承认她比自己更有义，揭露他没有履行责任。

sampleVerse.text: And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

explanation.en: Cain was Adam and Eve's first son, a farmer whose jealousy of Abel grew into the first recorded murder. Genesis 4:8 states that he attacked and killed his brother in the field after refusing God's warning about sin.
explanation.zh: 该隐是亚当和夏娃的长子，是一名农夫；他对亚伯的嫉妒发展为圣经记载的第一宗杀人。创世记4:8说他拒绝上帝对罪的警告后，在田间攻击并杀死兄弟。

sampleVerse.text: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

explanation.en: Micaiah son of Imlah was a faithful prophet who contradicted Ahab's flattering court prophets. First Kings 22:14 records his resolve to speak only what the LORD told him, even though truth would bring imprisonment.
explanation.zh: 音拉的儿子米该雅是忠心先知，敢于反对迎合亚哈的宫廷先知。列王纪上22:14记载他决意只说耶和华吩咐的话，即使真话会使他入狱。

sampleVerse.text: And Micaiah said, As the LORD liveth, what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.

explanation.en: Nineveh was the great Assyrian capital on the Tigris, notorious to Israel yet still addressed by God's warning. Jonah 3:5 records its people believing God and fasting in repentance, showing divine mercy reaching an enemy city.
explanation.zh: 尼尼微是底格里斯河畔的亚述大都，对以色列恶名昭彰，却仍得到上帝的警告。约拿书3:5记载城中人信服上帝并禁食悔改，显明上帝的怜悯也临到敌国之城。

sampleVerse.text: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

explanation.en: Eden was the garden region God prepared as the first human home, rich in life, beauty, and direct fellowship. Genesis 2:8 says God planted the garden and placed the man there, making it the setting for humanity's original vocation and test.
explanation.zh: 伊甸是上帝为最初人类预备的园地，充满生命、美丽和直接相交。创世记2:8说上帝栽种园子并把人安置其中，使它成为人类起初使命与考验的场所。

sampleVerse.text: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

explanation.en: Amon son of Manasseh became king of Judah and quickly continued the idolatry of his father's earlier years. Second Kings 21:20 judges his conduct as evil before the LORD, and his servants soon assassinated him.
explanation.zh: 玛拿西的儿子亚们作犹大王，很快继续父亲早年偶像崇拜的道路。列王纪下21:20判定他行耶和华眼中看为恶的事；不久臣仆便刺杀了他。

sampleVerse.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh did.

explanation.en: Ephesus was the chief city of Roman Asia and famous for the temple of Artemis, called Diana in the KJV. Acts 19:28 records craftsmen shouting for Diana during a riot because the gospel threatened their idolatrous trade.
explanation.zh: 以弗所是罗马亚细亚的首府，以亚底米神庙闻名，KJV 称这女神为 Diana。使徒行传19:28记载工匠因福音威胁偶像生意而骚乱，高喊女神的名。

sampleVerse.text: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

explanation.en: Kish was a wealthy Benjaminite and the father of Saul, Israel's first king. First Samuel 9:1 introduces his ancestry and standing immediately before Saul's search for lost donkeys leads to Samuel.
explanation.zh: 基士是富有的便雅悯人，也是以色列第一位君王扫罗的父亲。撒母耳记上9:1在扫罗寻找失驴并遇见撒母耳之前，先介绍他的家谱和地位。

sampleVerse.text: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.

explanation.en: Michal was Saul's daughter and David's first wife, whose relationship with him was shaped by love, royal conflict, and later estrangement. First Samuel 19:12 records her lowering David through a window to save him from Saul's killers.
explanation.zh: 米甲是扫罗的女儿和大卫的第一位妻子；两人的关系经历爱情、王室冲突和后来的疏离。撒母耳记上19:12记载她从窗户缒下大卫，使他逃离扫罗派来的杀手。

sampleVerse.text: So Michal let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.

explanation.en: Shem was one of Noah's three sons and ancestor of peoples including Abraham's family line. Genesis 9:26 blesses the LORD as the God of Shem, giving his descendants a distinctive place in the unfolding covenant story.
explanation.zh: 闪是挪亚三个儿子之一，也是包括亚伯拉罕家族在内多个民族的先祖。创世记9:26称颂耶和华为闪的上帝，使他的后裔在逐步展开的盟约历史中居于特别位置。

sampleVerse.text: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.

explanation.en: Horeb is a name for the Sinai mountain region where Moses met God and Israel received the covenant. Deuteronomy 5:2 says the LORD made a covenant with Israel there before Moses repeats the Ten Commandments.
explanation.zh: 何烈是西奈山地区的名称；摩西在那里遇见上帝，以色列也在那里领受盟约。申命记5:2在摩西重述十诫前说，耶和华曾在何烈山与以色列立约。

sampleVerse.text: The LORD our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.

explanation.en: Keilah was a fortified town in Judah's lowlands attacked by Philistine raiders. First Samuel 23:5 records David rescuing its inhabitants and their livestock, although the town would later be willing to surrender him to Saul.
explanation.zh: 基伊拉是犹大低地的坚城，曾受非利士掠夺者攻击。撒母耳记上23:5记载大卫救了居民和牲畜，尽管这城后来准备把他交给扫罗。

sampleVerse.text: So David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their cattle, and smote them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

explanation.en: Libnah was a Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands that later became a Levitical town. Joshua 10:29 records Joshua moving Israel's campaign there after the fall of Makkedah.
explanation.zh: 立拿是犹大低地的迦南王城，后来成为利未人的城。约书亚记10:29记载玛基大陷落后，约书亚把以色列的战役转向立拿。

sampleVerse.text: Then Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, unto Libnah, and fought against Libnah:

explanation.en: Meshach was the Babylonian name given to Mishael, one of Daniel's three Judean companions. Daniel 3:23 records him bound and cast into the fiery furnace for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's image, where God preserved him.
explanation.zh: 米煞是但以理三位犹大同伴之一米沙利所得的巴比伦名字。但以理书3:23记载他因拒绝敬拜尼布甲尼撒的像，被捆绑扔进火窑，却蒙上帝保全。

sampleVerse.text: And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace.

explanation.en: Asahel was David's nephew, Joab's younger brother, and a warrior famed for speed. Second Samuel 2:23 records Abner killing him after repeated warnings to stop pursuit, a death that fueled lasting blood vengeance.
explanation.zh: 亚撒黑是大卫的外甥、约押的弟弟，也是以奔跑迅速闻名的战士。撒母耳记下2:23记载他无视多次警告继续追赶，最终被押尼珥杀死，由此引发长期血仇。

sampleVerse.text: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

explanation.en: Kadesh-barnea was an oasis on Canaan's southern approach and a principal camp during Israel's wilderness years. Numbers 13:26 records the spies returning there with fruit and their report, after which unbelief delayed entry into the land.
explanation.zh: 加低斯巴尼亚是通往迦南南部的绿洲，也是以色列旷野年间的重要营地。民数记13:26记载探子带着果子和报告回到那里，随后百姓的不信使进入应许地被延迟。

sampleVerse.text: And they went and came to Moses, and to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word unto them, and unto all the congregation, and shewed them the fruit of the land.

explanation.en: Nadab was Aaron's eldest son and one of the first priests consecrated for sanctuary service. Leviticus 10:1 records him and Abihu offering unauthorized fire before the LORD, a fatal warning against treating holy worship casually.
explanation.zh: 拿答是亚伦的长子，也是最早受膏从事圣所事奉的祭司之一。利未记10:1记载他与亚比户献上未经吩咐的凡火，成为不可轻慢神圣敬拜的致命警戒。

sampleVerse.text: And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not.

explanation.en: Shallum son of Jabesh seized Israel's throne by killing Zechariah but held it only one month. Second Kings 15:13 dates that brief reign in Samaria before Menahem overthrew him.
explanation.zh: 雅比的儿子沙龙杀死撒迦利雅夺取以色列王位，却只统治一个月。列王纪下15:13记下他在撒玛利亚短暂的王权，随后便被米拿现推翻。

sampleVerse.text: Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria.

explanation.en: Abigail was Nabal's wise wife who later married David after preventing him from taking reckless vengeance. In 1 Samuel 25:33 David blesses her judgment for keeping him from bloodguilt and self-appointed revenge.
explanation.zh: 亚比该是拿八聪慧的妻子；她阻止大卫草率报仇，后来成为大卫的妻子。撒母耳记上25:33中，大卫称赞她的见识，因为她使自己免于流无辜人的血和擅自伸冤。

sampleVerse.text: And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand.

explanation.en: Ahijah of Shiloh was the prophet who announced that most of Solomon's kingdom would pass to Jeroboam. First Kings 11:31 interprets the torn garment as ten tribes taken from Solomon's house because of covenant unfaithfulness.
explanation.zh: 示罗人亚希雅是先知，宣告所罗门的大部分国土将归耶罗波安。列王纪上11:31以撕裂的衣服解释十个支派将从所罗门家夺去，原因是对盟约不忠。

sampleVerse.text: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:

explanation.en: Elkanah was a Levite living in Ephraim, husband of Hannah, and father of Samuel. First Samuel 1:3 describes his yearly journey to Shiloh for worship and sacrifice, the setting in which Hannah prayed for a son.
explanation.zh: 以利加拿是住在以法莲的利未人、哈拿的丈夫，也是撒母耳的父亲。撒母耳记上1:3描述他每年到示罗敬拜献祭，这也成为哈拿求子的背景。

sampleVerse.text: And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were there.

explanation.en: Hezron was a son of Perez and an ancestor in the royal line leading through Boaz and Jesse to David. Ruth 4:19 places him in the closing genealogy, connecting Ruth's restored family with Judah's earlier generations.
explanation.zh: 希斯仑是法勒斯的儿子，也是经波阿斯、耶西通向大卫之王族谱系的先祖。路得记4:19把他列在结尾家谱中，使路得得恢复的家庭与犹大早期世代相连。

sampleVerse.text: And Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,

explanation.en: Omri was an Israelite commander who won a civil struggle for the throne and founded a powerful northern dynasty. First Kings 16:24 records him buying the hill of Samaria and building the city that became Israel's capital.
explanation.zh: 暗利原是以色列将领，在争夺王位的内战中获胜，并建立强大的北国王朝。列王纪上16:24记载他买下撒玛利亚山，建造后来成为以色列首都的城市。

sampleVerse.text: And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria.

explanation.en: Tirzah was a beautiful Canaanite royal city that served as the northern kingdom's capital before Samaria. First Kings 14:17 records Jeroboam's wife returning there as their son dies according to Ahijah's word.
explanation.zh: 得撒是美丽的迦南王城，在撒玛利亚建成前曾作北国首都。列王纪上14:17记载耶罗波安的妻子回到那里时，儿子按亚希雅的话死去。

sampleVerse.text: And Jeroboam's wife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah: and when she came to the threshold of the door, the child died;

explanation.en: Zerah the Ethiopian led a vast army against Judah during King Asa's reign. Second Chronicles 14:9 records his advance to Mareshah, where Asa sought God and the invading force was defeated.
explanation.zh: 古实人谢拉在亚撒王时期率领大军攻打犹大。历代志下14:9记载他进到玛利沙；亚撒在那里求告上帝，入侵军最终战败。

sampleVerse.text: And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came unto Mareshah.

explanation.en: Hazor was the leading Canaanite city of northern Palestine and headed the coalition defeated by Joshua near Lake Merom. Joshua 11:10 calls it the head of those kingdoms and records Israel taking its king.
explanation.zh: 夏琐是迦南北部的主要城市，领导了在米伦水边被约书亚击败的联盟。约书亚记11:10称它素来是诸国之首，并记载以色列擒获其王。

sampleVerse.text: And Joshua at that time turned back, and took Hazor, and smote the king thereof with the sword: for Hazor beforetime was the head of all those kingdoms.

explanation.en: Silas, also called Silvanus, was a respected Jerusalem believer, prophet, and missionary companion of Paul. Acts 15:40 records Paul choosing him for a journey that strengthened churches after the separation from Barnabas.
explanation.zh: 西拉又称西瓦努（Silvanus），是受尊重的耶路撒冷信徒、先知和保罗的宣教同工。使徒行传15:40记载保罗与巴拿巴分开后选择西拉同行，去坚固众教会。

sampleVerse.text: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.
